blocks.text: Pacific Punk Wave is a visual design movement prominent from the late 1970s and 1980s that mixes Pacific New Wave music, punk rebellion, Italian radical design and Swiss New Wave typography. It was heavily influenced by interior, post- modern graphics, and fashion trends, serving as a precursor to styles like New Wave Tropical and Memphis Lite. It paved the way for the 1980s/1990s post-modern commercial aesthetic, inspiring digital design revivals like vector graphics and synthwave.
Messy & Eclectic Layouts: Embraced irregular borders, horror vacui (a fear of space), and overlapping abstract shapes.
Bold/Textured Gradients: Featured solid, flat blocks of color, opting instead for stippled, airbrushed, or striped pattern fills.
Kitschy-Retro Revival: Included mid-century modern, playful, Googie architecture elements, and 1950s pop-culture kitsch.
Hand-Drawn Edge: Incorporated sketchy, raw, or misaligned geometrical/line art that broke traditional corporate design rules.
